rounds.text: Kross Ltd demonstrates exceptional fundamental growth, underscored by a phenomenal 5-year compounded profit growth of 64% and a trailing twelve-month profit growth of 40% [E17, E19]. This powerful earnings trajectory is supported by robust top-line expansion, including a 5-year compounded sales growth of 30% and a 36% surge over the trailing twelve months [E14, E16]. The company generates superior returns compared to its peers, with an ROCE of 15.29% outperforming the sector benchmark of 12.7% and an ROA of 7.86% beating the 6.37% benchmark [E8, E10]. Valuation and intrinsic metrics further highlight undervaluation, as a discounted cash flow analysis puts intrinsic value at Rs 437 per share against a market price of Rs 298, offering a 31.8% margin of safety [E38, E39]. Moreover, the reverse DCF indicates that today's price implies only 12.7% earnings growth, which is considerably conservative against the base case assumption of 18.0% [E40]. Insider confidence is evident through promoters increasing their stake to 68.57% in Sep 2026 from 67.70% in Sep 2024, alongside a rules-based screen scoring the stock 93 out of 100 with a BUY rating [E34, E56]. conceded: [E28] and [E30] and [E55].

A critical examination of the financials reveals severe cash generation and working capital disconnects that undermine the reported earnings growth. Profits are running far ahead of actual cash collection, evidenced by a dismal cash conversion ratio of 0.51x for March 2026 [E28], which directly results in a staggering negative free cash flow of Rs -72 Cr [E30]. This cash burn coincides with a dramatic lengthening of working capital days from 86.9 days to 124 days [E55], signaling mounting operational friction and trapped liquidity. Debt financing is accelerating rapidly to plug these gaps, with borrowings doubling to Rs 119 Cr in Sep 2026 from Rs 54 Cr a year prior [E32], alongside a massive 243.8% surge in capital-tied construction work in progress [E33]. Meanwhile, institutional confidence is visibly retreating, as both foreign and domestic institutional investors have cut their holdings over the past two years [E35, E36], leaving retail and promoters to shoulder an extended stock trading near its 52-week peak with a 0.00% dividend yield [E4, E41, E54]. Conceded: the company demonstrates strong trailing sales and profit growth alongside robust headline returns on capital [E16, E19, E12], and institutional money flow registers as positive overall [E37].

However, this cash burn and the 243.8% surge in construction work in progress to Rs 55 Cr [E33] reflect an active capital expenditure build-up phase for growth rather than structural distress, supported by a conservative debt-to-equity ratio of just 0.23x [E31]. The lengthening of working capital days [E55] occurs alongside compounding sales growth of 36% over the trailing twelve months [E16] and an exceptional rules-based screen score of 93 out of 100 [E56]. Finally, the absence of a dividend yield [E4] is entirely consistent with a high-growth business aggressively reinvesting its profits to drive 40% compounded profit growth in the trailing twelve months [E19].

Finally, leaning on high momentum while annualised volatility sits at a punishing 55.4% [E47] overlooks the bias checklist warning that chasing extended stocks near their 52-week highs without defined risk is how concentrated conviction turns into severe drawdowns [E61, E62].
